bio: What is most striking is its location in the Art al Camp, a natural-artistic outdoor space with a series of charming palm trees, olive trees and large wrought iron figures, the works of local sculptor Toni Marí and Juan Ripollés; in fact, visible from the road, we are welcomed by Antonia, a sculpture measuring more than 30 metres... in the shape of a whale! In the bright, contemporary restaurant, chef Alejandro Crespo adopts a Mediterranean-inspired cuisine that stands out for its modern take on tapas (such as Nuestro mejillón tigre (stuffed mussels)), the extensive Cocas de La Marina section and, above all, its delicious rice dishes (make sure to try the Prawn and pumpkin meloso or the Figatell and chickpea fideuá). Reservations are recommended, especially in summer to eat on the terrace!
